---
title: "Introduction to mapSpainHist"
description: "First steps: municipal maps of a census, census figures and changes over time."
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, dpi = 110,
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dev.args = list(bg = "white"),
  eval = !is.null(suppressMessages(mapSpainHist:::mhist_geometry_file()))
)
```

**mapSpainHist** provides the municipal boundaries of Spain for each population census between
1900 and 2001, together with the figures of those censuses. This article shows how to get the maps,
how to represent data on them and how to follow municipal changes over time.

> **Warning.** The shape of most historical municipalities is an approximate reconstruction. The
> maps are useful above all to represent municipal data; use them with caution for geographic
> variables such as area or distances. See the [methodology](methodology.html).

## Installation and first load

```{r, eval = FALSE}
remotes::install_github("pauvallprat/mapSpainHist")
```

```{r}
library(mapSpainHist)
library(ggplot2)
```

The available censuses are:

```{r}
mhist_census_years()
```

The function `esp_get_munic_hist()` returns an `sf` object with one polygon for each municipality
in force at the given census. The first time it downloads the geometries from Zenodo (about
6.5 MB) and stores them in a local cache; afterwards it reads them directly from disk.

```{r}
m1930 <- esp_get_munic_hist(1930)
nrow(m1930)
head(sf::st_drop_geometry(m1930))
```

Each row has the INE code of the municipality (`cod_ine`), the census figures (name, province,
autonomous community, judicial district, households and de jure and de facto population) and the
geometry. Non-municipal territories (common pastures, *facerías*, etc., with codes 53xxx) have
`no_munic = 1` and no census figures; they can be dropped with `include_nonmunicipal = FALSE`.

## A population map

We represent the de jure population of each municipality in 1930. With `moveCAN = TRUE` the Canary
Islands are placed next to the Peninsula, as the **mapSpain** package does. In this case it is
advisable to draw the box that separates them too, with `mapSpain::esp_get_can_box()`.

```{r map-1930, fig.alt = "Map of the municipalities of Spain in 1930 coloured by de jure population"}
m1930 <- esp_get_munic_hist(1930, moveCAN = TRUE)
m1930$population <- cut(
  m1930$pder, c(0, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 20000, Inf), right = FALSE,
  labels = c("< 500", "500-999", "1,000-1,999", "2,000-4,999", "5,000-19,999", "20,000 or more")
)

ggplot(m1930) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = population), colour = NA) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "magma", direction = -1, na.value = "grey85") +
  geom_sf(data = mapSpain::esp_get_can_box(), colour = "grey50") +
  labs(title = "De jure population by municipality, 1930", fill = "Inhabitants") +
  theme_void()
```

## Municipalities throughout the 20th century

The `censos` table contains the figures of every municipality and every census between 1842 and
2011. A municipality is in force at a census when it has household figures (`hogares`). We can
count how many municipalities there were at each census:

```{r}
inforce <- censos[!is.na(censos$hogares) & censos$censo %in% mhist_census_years(), ]
table(inforce$censo)
```

The sharp drop in the 1960s and 1970s corresponds to the municipal mergers of those years. As each
map contains exactly the municipalities in force at its census, these changes can be followed on
the ground. For example, Valdetórtola (Cuenca) was created in the 1970s from several municipalities
and dissolved in the 1990s:

```{r valdetortola, fig.height = 3.6, fig.alt = "Three maps (1970, 1981 and 1991) of the area of Valdetórtola, in Cuenca, which only exists in 1981"}
m81 <- esp_get_munic_hist(1981, epsg = 3035, census_data = FALSE)
area_vt <- sf::st_buffer(m81[m81$cod_ine == "16907", ], 12000)

maps <- lapply(c(1970, 1981, 1991), function(y) {
  m <- esp_get_munic_hist(y, epsg = 3035, census_data = FALSE)
  m <- m[lengths(sf::st_intersects(m, area_vt)) > 0, ]
  m$census <- y
  m
})
d <- do.call(rbind, maps)

ggplot(d) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = cod_ine == "16907"), colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey92", `TRUE` = "tomato"),
                    labels = c("Other municipalities", "Valdetórtola"), name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~census) +
  theme_void()
```

## Adding your own data

To represent your own data (for example, election results or figures from another census), just
join them by the INE code, `cod_ine`, a 5-character string:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
mydata <- read.csv("municipal_data_1930.csv", colClasses = c(cod_ine = "character"))
m1930 <- merge(esp_get_munic_hist(1930), mydata, by = "cod_ine", all.x = TRUE)
```

To aggregate data to provinces, judicial districts or electoral districts, see the article
[Higher-level units and data aggregation](units.html).

## Cache

The geometries are stored in the directory returned by `mhist_cache_dir()`. It can be changed for
the session with `mhist_set_cache_dir()` or with the `cache_dir` argument of the functions, and
emptied with `mhist_clear_cache()`. The argument `update_cache = TRUE` forces a new download.

```{r}
mhist_cache_dir()
```
